sentences.text:
The PSI of Basaveshwaranagara Police Station has laid charge sheet against accused Nos.1 & 2 for the offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
2.

THE PROSECUTION'S CASE IN NUTSHELL IS AS UNDER:
That, on 21.05.2022, at 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop,
situated at No.222, 7 th Cross, 1st Main, Manjunathnagar 1st Phase, the accused No.1 having drawn the attention of PW-1 by requesting PW-1 to pack Dry Fruits weighing half KG each, persuaded PW-1 to handover her golden mangalasutra on the pretext of the design of the said chain being nicely crafted, the accused No.1 has stolen the said golden mangalasutra and ran away from the said shop and thereafter handed over the said mangalasutra to accused No.2 to dispose the same, thereby the accused No.1 has committed offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
3.

On receipt of First Information Statement by the complainant/CW-1, Basaveshwaranagar Police have registered the case in Cr. No.79/2022 for the offences punishable U/s.379 & 420 of IPC and transmitted the FIR to the jurisdictional Magistrate.
After completion of investigation, the IO has filed the final report against the accused Nos.1 & 2 for having committed the offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
4. Thereafter, my predecessor in office after careful examination of the charge sheet and prosecution papers has taken cognizance of offences U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
5. On service of summons, the accused No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed bail application.
The same was considered and he has been enlarged on bail.

7. After appearance of accused No.1, charge sheet copy, statement of the witnesses and documents along with charge sheet has been supplied to the accused No.1 in compliance of Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.

Thereafter, my predecessor in office has heard the learned Sr. APP and counsel for accused No.1 and framed charge by reading over and explaining the allegations of prosecution to the accused No.1 for the offences punishable U/s.379, 420 & 414 of IPC.
The accused No.1 has not pleaded guilty and claimed to be tried.
8. The prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked five documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-5 and closed its side of evidence.

The statement of the accused No.1 as contemplated U/s.313 of Cr.P.C., is dispensed as there is no any incriminating materials appearing against him and submitted that he has no any defence evidence on his behalf.
9. Heard both the sides.
Perused final report, oral and documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution.

10. On the basis of the above, the following points arise for consideration of this court viz.,
1) Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubts that, on 21.05.2022, at about 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop, situated at No.222, 7th Cross, 1st Main,
Manjunathnagar 3rd Phase, the accused No.1, having been to the said shop, on the pretext of purchasing the dry fruits, by gaining confidence of PW-1 so also by distracting her attention, made her to remove her golden mangalasutra weighing about 32 grams and stolen the same and thereby accused No.1 committed an offence punishable U/s.379 of IPC?
2) Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubts that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused No.1, by having gained the confidence of PW-1 by conversing with her husband in connection to purchase of dry fruits so also having distracted the attention of PW-1, by ordering to pack 500 grams of various dry fruits, while PW-1 had handed over her mangalasutra, by having stolen the said managalasutra with an ulterior intention to deceive the PW-1 and thereby accused No.1 committed an offence punishable U/s.420 of IPC?
3) Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubts that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused No.1 by having handed over the stolen mangalasutra of PW-1 to the accused No.2 to dispose the said chain and thereby accused No.1 committed an offence punishable U/s.414 of IPC?
4) What order?
11. On the basis of the oral and documentary evidence, the findings of this court to the above point is as under:

3  Point No.2 : In the Negative  Point No.3 : In the Negative  Point No.4 : As per final order  for the following  REASONS 12. Point Nos.1 to 3:
All these points are interlinked to each other.
In order to avoid repetition of facts, these points are taken up for discussion together.

13. The prosecution burdened to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts has got examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked five documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-5.
14.

It is the prosecution's case that, on 21.05.2022, at 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop, situated at No.222, 7th Cross, 1st Main, Manjunathnagar 1st Phase, the accused No.1 having drawn the attention of PW-1 by requesting PW-1 to pack Dry Fruits weighing half KG each,
persuaded PW-1 to handover her golden mangalasutra on the pretext of the design of the said chain being nicely crafted, the accused No.1 has stolen the said golden mangalasutra and ran away from the said shop and thereafter handed over the said mangalasutra to accused No.2 to dispose the same, thereby the accused No.1 has committed offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
15. CW-1, who is cited as victim/complainant is examined as PW-1 and she has accounted as to having lodged the FIS at Basaveshwaranagara PS in connection to the theft of her mangalasutra.
She has also accounted as to having affixed her signature on the document styled as spot mahazar at the request of police officials.
The said FIS and spot mahazar are marked as Ex.P-1 and Ex.P-2 and signatures are marked as Ex.P-1(a) and Ex.P-2(a) respectively.
Further, she has accounted regarding her golden mangalasutra being traced and handed over to her on 24.06.2022.
The property released panchanama bearing signature of the witness is marked as Ex.P-3 and her signature is marked as Ex.P-3(a).
She has pleaded ignorance regarding the contents of Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-3 so also the signatories to the Ex.P-2 & Ex.P-3.
She has failed to identify the accused No.1 before the court and also denied regarding statements being given by her to the police officials in connection to the case on hand.

16. PW-1 is treated as hostile witness and permitted to be cross-examined by the learned Sr. APP,
the endeavor on her part to elicit the prosecution's case as per the FIS and spot mahazar so also prosecution papers by confronting their contents to PW-1 so also the accused No.1 in person has turned futile exercise.
The specific suggestions as to the accused No.1 has been confronted to her by the police officials on 07.06.2022 has been denied by the witness.

The denied portion in the voluntary statements of the PW-1 insofar as the weight of golden mangalasutra dated 22.05.2022 as well as confrontation of accused No.1 at police station on 07.06.2022 are marked as Ex.P-4 and Ex.P-5 respectively.

sentences.text: As the victim/complainant has deposed contrary to the prosecution papers, the prayer of learned Sr. APP for issuance of witness summons to other prosecution witnesses has been rejected.

18. An anxious examination of prosecution papers, evidence on record and arguments canvassed by the learned Sr. APP and the counsel for the accused No.1, this court has to examine the prosecution's allegations as to the CW-1's golden mangalasutra weighing 36 grams being stolen by accused No.1 by distracting her attention with an ulterior intention to deceive PW-1 and the said chain being handed over to accused No.2 to dispose for making unlawful gain.

19. It is pertinent to note that, the testimony of victim/complainant, who has deposed contrary to the prosecution's case insofar as identification of accused No.1 is crucial aspect which goes to the root of the matter.

Furthermore, the testimony of said PW-1 in having not given the statement in connection to confrontation of accused No.1 by the Investigating Officer on 07.06.2022, cannot be considered to appreciate the prosecution's claim put-forth in the case on hand.

That apart, the involvement of accused No.1 in the case on hand is unable to be gathered, as the PW-1 has very much denied the identification of accused No.1, which is a crucial aspect as per Ex.P-5.
20.

It is also pertinent to note that, the prosecution's case is unable to be gathered as the FIS fails to narrate the description insofar as appearance of miscreant involved in the case on hand as well as the details of the motorcycle involved creates a doubt in the mind of the court.
That apart, FIS is also not specific insofar as the description of the individual involved in the case on hand.
In absence of relevant details pertaining to the miscreant insofar as their age, their facial looks, body marks will not be sufficient to fix the criminal guilt.

21. That apart, the arguments of the prosecution as to accused No.1 had intention to deceive the PW-1 as such he distracted the attention of PW-1 and also infurtherence of the said intention to deceive handed over the golden mangalasutra to accused No.2 in itself cannot be appreciated as the PW-1 has failed to identify regarding the involvement of accused No.1 in the case on hand.

22. In the case on hand, overall examination of testimony of the prosecution witness and prosecution papers, this court is justified to opine that the prosecution's case is tainted with substantial improvements, omissions and contradictions.
It is needless to point out that the very ingredients of the alleged offences are unable to be gathered from the testimony of the material prosecution witness.
This court without any hesitation holds prosecution has miserably failed to bring home guilt of the accused No.1 beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly this court proceeds to answer Point Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative.
23. Point No.4:

In view of the above findings on point Nos.1 to 3, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 379, 420 & 414 of IPC.
Consequently, accused No.1 is set at liberty.
